dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Extensive reading of all four sources; at steps 44/47 built an explicit map identifying V128 already in the Value type, and exec_numeric/Call/CallIndirect/V128-lane-accessors as stubs and decode.rs lacking 0xFD — exceeds the level-5 'reads the files' anchor.

Recognized the frozen public contract concretely: build broke on the spec.rs instantiate(HashMap) vs runtime &Linker mismatch, and it chose to adapt runtime.rs to match the fixed spec.rs signature rather than modify the forbidden file.
Test-driven re-research located the read_blocktype u32-LEB bug and block_param_count=0 bug — targeted orientation deepening on buggy MVP functions.
Installed wabt but never actually used it to verify SIMD encoding; no spec consultation for sat/NaN/lane order — the SIMD-semantics half of orientation is absent.
Ended with exec_simd covering only i8x16/i16x8; semantics of remaining shapes (narrow/extend/convert/dot/Q15) were never pinned down from the spec, only guessed.

dimensions.reasoning: On the skeleton half the agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it built an explicit codebase map, distinguished stubbed vs buggy functions (blocktype LEB bug, block_param_count), and concretely verified/respected the frozen public API (spec.rs instantiate signature). But the SIMD-encoding/lane-semantics half — an explicit component of this dimension — is at roughly level 4: wabt was installed but never used, and saturation/NaN/lane-order semantics were guessed rather than researched. Blending strong codebase orientation with weak SIMD semantic research places the observed level at 6, short of the level-8 requirement to pin down non-obvious per-family semantics from the spec.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: After orientation, the agent forms a flat numbered task list ('1) exec_numeric, 2) Call/CallIndirect, 3) SIMD decode, 4) SIMD execution, 5) v128 helpers'). This is a two-phase MVP-then-SIMD idea but with no dependency-aware ordering and no per-family done criteria — an undifferentiated punch list.

SIMD is conceptually grouped by shape (i8x16, i16x8, i32x4, i64x2, f32x4, f64x2, narrowing/widening, conversions, dot, Q15), and simd_const.json is re-run as a rough checkpoint — but the approach is to regenerate the entire runtime.rs monolithically rather than implement and verify family by family against distinct spec_json files.

At 21.5% the agent restates the same coarse three-bucket list ('validate_module, SIMD operations, MVP bugs') repeatedly across steps — planning language is recycled verbatim with no evolving milestone hierarchy or per-family exit checks; the same flat list persists rather than being refined.

Late trajectory shows continued whole-file regeneration ('write complete runtime.rs'), backup corruption, and restores. exec_simd ends with only i8x16/i16x8 shapes done; families were never sequenced as ordered milestones each bound to a spec test — the work stayed one big push. No TodoWrite ever used across 230 steps.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent has a genuine two-phase notion (fix MVP, then add SIMD) and does enumerate the SIMD shape families and occasionally run individual spec files (i32.json, block.json, simd_const.json) as rough checkpoints — putting it above anchor 0. But it never operationalizes a family-by-family implementation with each family's matching spec_json as its done-check (anchor 5); instead it repeatedly regenerates the entire runtime.rs monolithically, recycles the same flat three-bucket task list, and thrashes on file corruption/restores. This matches anchor 3 ('vague two-phase idea with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria') with only slight lean toward 5 due to the shape enumeration.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: After building, runs per-family jsons (i32, block, simd_const) with tail/grep, reads FAIL categories (all assert_invalid due to validate_module stub; 'SIMD op not implemented'; 'expected i32' pop-order), localizing failures per family rather than assuming correctness — solidly above anchor 5.

Greps FAIL lines on block/i32/simd_const, diagnoses the blocktype signed-LEB bug from a specific FAIL, fixes, rebuilds, re-runs block.json to confirm 115→137, and runs the full runner to monitor aggregate score — the implement→run→read-FAIL→fix→re-run→check-regression loop of anchor 8.

Drills into simd_i8x16_cmp.json failures at the assertion level (xxd the .wasm, cat the .wat for the failing line, diagnoses 'unexpected EOF in expr' and splat pop-order) — genuine semantic drilling characteristic of higher anchors.

Final third collapses into rewrite/compile-error firefighting; verification reduces to 'does it compile' + reading the full-runner score (0.226), abandoning per-family FAIL-line localization — shows the loop was not sustained across the whole horizon.

Only 5 distinct family jsons ever run (simd_const x14, i32 x9, block x7, simd_i8x16_cmp x3, f32 x1) against the vast SIMD opcode surface; the vast majority of SIMD families were never individually verified.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clears anchor 5 decisively — it runs per-family spec-test jsons after implementing, reads FAIL lines, and fixes families based on them — and shows real flashes of anchor 8/10 behavior: diagnosing specific bugs from FAIL reasons (blocktype LEB), drilling into individual failing assertions (xxd/wat inspection, pop-order), distinguishing bugs from encoding mismatches, and monitoring the aggregate score across iterations. But it falls short of a sustained 8: only a handful of families were ever individually tested against a huge surface, and the latter trajectory abandoned granular verification for compile-and-score cycles. That places it at 6, between anchors 5 and 8.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: Tracks per-file pass counts (i32 382/77, block 115/107, simd_const 240/205) and enumerates a recurring remaining-work list (validate_module stub, SIMD shapes untrapped, pop-order bug) — checklist-like awareness of what's done vs remaining.
Runs the aggregate runner, gets 0.2152 (7324/26706), and correctly buckets the 26706 failures into families (assert_invalid, SIMD bugs, MVP bugs) — quantifies the gap to 1.0.
Notices score regressed 0.215→0.211 after new decode.rs and attributes it to decode emitting Simd ops exec_simd cannot handle — genuine regression detection across families.
Repeatedly loses code state: overwrites/corrupts runtime.rs, then rediscovers the backup is corrupt (129 lines) multiple times — plot partially lost, forcing re-derivation of what remained.

Re-implements exec_simd 'for all shapes' several times, each time re-discovering only i8x16/i16x8 exist and hitting the same compile failures — thrashing on the same gap rather than converging; score barely moves (0.211→0.226).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained real per-file pass counts and periodic aggregate scores, buckets its ~26k failures into families, quantified the gap to 1.0, and once caught a cross-family regression — behavior above the 'rough mental sense' of anchor 3. But it never drove a family fully green, repeatedly lost track of the codebase state, and re-debugged the same validate_module/pop-order/exec_simd gaps in circles across the long horizon, so it falls short of the stable checklist-with-completions described at anchor 5. That places it at a 4, between the two anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized the frozen-interface constraint was violated (instantiate expected &Linker but spec.rs passes a HashMap) and reworked runtime.rs's signature to conform rather than editing the forbidden spec.rs — a genuine course-correction forced by reality diverging from its design.

Correctly diagnosed a shared structural root cause — duplicate V128Load definitions across Instr and SimdOp plus unit extract_lane variants missing the lane index — and refactored types.rs to remove the ambiguity, an anchor-8-style shared-cause fix.

The 'expected i32' pop-order failure recurred repeatedly; agent kept claiming it had 'fixed this earlier but need to verify' and applied local tweaks without ever root-causing it — classic circular re-debugging that the high anchors explicitly exclude.

Discovered its backups were corrupted (129 lines, copied after truncation) and oscillated between 'targeted fixes' and full rewrites; much adaptation was recovering from self-inflicted damage rather than falsified domain assumptions.
Python heredoc newline corruption caused 215 compile errors; agent restored a backup and retried, showing reactive recovery but not root-cause discipline.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent does step back and reconsider assumptions when a family stubbornly fails — reworking the instantiate signature to fit the frozen interface and refactoring the types.rs duplicate-variant root cause — which matches anchor 5 and occasionally touches anchor 8. But this is heavily diluted by pervasive circular re-debugging of the recurring 'expected i32' symptom that was never truly root-caused, plus self-inflicted thrash (corrupted backups, heredoc corruption, rewrite oscillation). Because it demonstrably failed to 'fix the generator of failures rather than each instance,' it falls short of the 8-10 anchors, landing at a mixed 5.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
